# Fagus sylvatica
_**Fagus sylvatica**_, the **European beech** or **common beech**, is a large [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous) tree in the [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagaceae) family with smooth silvery-grey bark, large leaf area, and a short trunk with low branches. [[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-3) It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.

## Distribution and habitat
The European beech is the most abundant hardwood species in Austrian, German and Swiss forests. [[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-11) The native range extends from the north, in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark), [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland), [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria), western [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine), and [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania), through Europe to [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France), southern [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England), Spain (on the [Cantabrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantabrian_Mountains), [Iberian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistema_Ib%C3%A9rico) and [Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistema_Central) mountain ranges),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-12) [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-13) and east to northwest [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-POWO-2) where it exhibits an interspecific [cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cline_(biology)) with the oriental beech ( _[Fagus orientalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_orientalis)_), which replaces it further east.

In Norway's oceanic climate planted trees grow well north to [Bodø Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bod%C3%B8_Municipality), and produce seedlings and can spread naturally in Trondheim.

One of the most beautiful European beech forests called [Sonian Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonian_Forest) ( _Forêt de Soignes/Zoniënwoud_) is found in the southeast of Brussels, Belgium. Beech is a dominant tree species in France and constitutes about 10% of French forests.

2. Fagus sylvatica (Beech) is a large usually single-stemmed deciduous tree native to south-east England but now growing over almost the whole of the British Isles, often planted as a forestry tree on all but the wettest soils. It forms extensive woodlands, where it is dominant over a large altitudinal range, competing primarily with Quercus robur. It is monoecious, wind-pollinated and notable for its periodic large seed numbers (mast years); seed is dispersed by birds and mammals but mostly drops below the parent tree.
